what_happened: Job 20261030-013421-tfwf (code job: "Give OLY-B-O5-02 a mechanism: restart cost, loss and fixes in status") failed in planning, before any code was written. The critic judged after round 1 that the reading misread the request, and the plan still needed revising at the last round (5 of 5). One major finding: the reading maps "the causes are fixed in Athena" to the restart record's `via` field. The code documents `--via` as what the new context read to resume, so it does not record a fix. The plan would count `via` entries (the existing lifecycle test has `via: ["athena status"]`) as fixes and make status claim causes were fixed when nothing records that. The fix needs its own field (an optional `fixed` with a serde default) or the claim should be dropped. Three minor findings: the new test file status_restarts.rs is not among the deliverables; minutes and tokens are summed across estimated and measured values without saying which is which; and if the fix moves to a new field, the dependents list must cover the record schema and the CLI argument. The plan's structure was otherwise sound. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that named files and seams exist, but nothing checks that a field the reading reuses actually means what the requirement needs. The reading matched the words "fixed in Athena" to a field by name and plausibility without reading the field's documented purpose at main.rs:450. The plan then built its mechanism, text and demonstration on that mapping. Planning has fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan and has no repair step, so a major finding that survives round 5 loses all planning spend. The critic's finding was a mechanical fix: add an optional field.
other_causes: The record schema had no field for fixes, so the requirement could not be met without a schema addition. The reading did not recognize that gap.
Planning has no repair step, so a single well-defined major finding at the last round fails the job.
open_hypotheses: The stored fields do not show whether the critic's round 1 finding was already raised and the planner failed to act on it in rounds 2 to 4, or whether the finding changed between rounds.
The fields do not show how much planning spend was lost.
contradictions: The critic found the plan's structure sound and the other field mappings (cost, minutes, tokens, lost) correct. Only the fix mapping was wrong, which points to a narrow slip rather than a broad failure of the reading.
prevention: Add a reading-stage check: when the reading maps a requirement onto an existing struct field, CLI argument or record key, it must quote that field's documented meaning from the code and state why it matches. A mismatch, or a requirement with no matching field, must become a schema-addition deliverable (new optional field with serde default, CLI argument, dependents). Run this before the plan is built, so a semantic mismatch is caught in round 1 and not carried through five rounds.
proposed_request: Give OLY-B-O5-02 a mechanism: show restart cost, loss and fixes in athena status. Build on the O5-01 restart record. Show restart cost (minutes and tokens, with estimated and measured values kept apart), what was lost, and whether the cause was fixed in Athena. Do not use `via` for fixes: it records what the new context read to resume. Add an optional `fixed` field to the restart record with a serde default, and a matching CLI argument on restart. Add a separate `restart review` label and StatusView field that satisfy every_measure_label_names_a_status_view_field_and_a_printed_line. Count a restart as fixed only when `fixed` is set. Add the test file crates/athena-cli/tests/status_restarts.rs to the deliverables, with a spec test modelled on oly_b_o5_01, and an end-to-end demonstration through Manager::restart, Athena::status and display::status. List the record schema and the CLI argument as dependents. Acceptance: fmt, clippy and test pass; an existing restart with only `via` is shown as having no recorded fix; a restart with `fixed` set is counted as fixed; CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
